content.comment_body: Hello, I am working with two [product_name] devices ([article_no]) in a master-master configuration alongside a [product_name]. My goal is to modify certain low/high setpoints through the [product_name] and have these updated setpoints remain stored, even if both devices are powered off for extended periods (months). I tested using a VM to transfer the setpoints via an analog comparator on/off mechanism, mapping them to a VM parameter. After several hours without power, the values I had modified were still retained. Could you clarify if VM is saved in EEPROM? If not, can VM be reliably used for long-term data storage, and does it require a battery for extended power-off durations? Is there a preferred method for retaining setpoints after a shutdown? Thank you, [user_name]
Hello, What you have found is correct. All parameters in [product_name] are retained. No battery is required except for older [product_name] models (up to [article_no]) for saving date and time.

Thank you [user_name] for your response. So it seems I need to use a block in [product_name] with parameters to store these values, although it may not be the most refined solution. I'm still uncertain about the optimal approach. I want to be able to change and keep alarm setpoints (like tank levels, motor water temperature, oil pressure, etc). From what I see, it's not possible to reliably save these changed values on the [product_name], which is a drawback. Storing values in [product_name] seems to be the only option. I'm also deciding whether to have [product_name] or the [product_name] handle the alarm monitoring. The [product_name] contains built-in alarm features such as delay, deadband, and visualization, but it does not seem straightforward to disable alarms (I want to avoid engine alarms when the engine is off). The benefit of having [product_name] monitor alarm values is that detection will be consistent, even if the [product_name] fails. Any further insights are welcome. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The user is looking for a solution to update and retain alarm setpoints, modified through a [product_name], across power cycles in a [product_name] setup. There is some uncertainty regarding data persistence capabilities of both devices, as well as practical methods for storing and monitoring changes. The discussion revolves around reliable data retention and decisions about which device should manage alarms.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects a reliable and straightforward method for permanently storing alarm setpoints changed via [product_name], even after long power outages, without resorting to workarounds that could risk data loss. They value flexibility in choosing which device handles alarm monitoring.
